requests.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit / missing intermediate camera view for reconstruction.
Image 1 is the CANONICAL ORIGINAL canal photograph and primary edit target. Image 2 is an existing much closer doorway view of the same cafe, a later viewpoint reference. Generate ONE intermediate photograph A, halfway along the WALK from camera 1 toward that cafe entrance, BEFORE reaching camera 2. This is a consistency experiment, so exact architectural/texture correspondence is more important than adding detail.

CAMERA:
Walk forward on the same left-bank pavement and gently toward the original red-awning cafe, at unchanged eye height and focal length. Move about halfway in physical travel distance between the two provided viewpoints; do not simply crop/zoom image 1 or copy the close-up framing of image 2. Aim slightly toward the cafe as in the original view. The complete burgundy awning, the cafe's wooden entrance and flanking glazed bays, the entire neighbouring teal storefront and some of the olive storefront must remain visible; keep the stone arched bridge on the far RIGHT side and enough riverbank to connect this image back to the original. This should be visibly CLOSER than image 1 yet clearly FARTHER than image 2, with true perspective/parallax and no new layout.
Use the original field of view, normal rectilinear lens, no fisheye, panorama, mirroring or invented camera tilt. Landscape 16:9.

IMMUTABLE LANDMARKS:
Keep the EXACT original cream stucco facade, burgundy awning shape and mounting points, round black hanging sign and its bracket, wooden doorframe/window mullion layout, upper-storey shutters and windows, adjacent teal then olive shops, fixed sidewalk paving border, bridge arch and bank attachments. Preserve existing wall marks, lamp brackets, window frame junctions and the exact number of openings so feature points can be matched across images. Do not repaint the building in a similar style: retain the same local surface identity and textures wherever visible. Retain bicycles and outdoor round table/chairs at the same locations; apparent changes come only from projection.
Keep the original cafe door CLOSED as in image 1; do not use opening the door as a way to alter the doorframe or neighboring windows. Image 2's open leaf is a later action, not a different entrance. The original visible interior through the glass stays in place; no extra doors, extra window panes, renamed shop, rearranged shelves or new props.
Image 1 governs the exterior if input 2 disagrees. Preserve the same blue-hour sky, warm lighting, exposure, wet stone material appearance and lamp positions. Only newly revealed surfaces should be inferred.
Output ONE clean photorealistic image, no labels, text, arrows, border, multi-panel or collage.

Use case: precise-object-edit / missing doorway transition for spatial consistency.
Image 1 is the existing exterior CLOSE DOORWAY photo, the authoritative front-wall/doorframe edit target.
Image 2 is the existing threshold-looking-IN interior, authoritative for furniture, shelves and pendant identities.
Image 3 is the just-generated intermediate WALK-UP exterior A, auxiliary exterior reference.
Make ONE missing transition photo B between images 1 and 2. It must depict the SAME rigid cafe, not a new cafe or montage.

CAMERA AND OVERLAP:
The camera takes only a short step from image 1 to the street-facing edge of the entrance threshold, at most 0.15m inside the front wall, at the same eye height and focal length. Turn gently toward the interior, halfway between image 1's oblique view and image 2's inward view. The image must still include the ORIGINAL door's full fixed wooden jamb and transom on at least one side, part of the adjoining glazed bay, the open leaf at its existing inward angle, and the first part of the LEFT service counter plus its distinctive objects. A small sliver of wet outdoor stone at the bottom/edge should meet the unchanged wood parquet threshold. Do not skip directly to a deep room-wide view.
Maintain a useful overlap with BOTH reference images: same fixed wood frame junctions from image 1 and same counter edge/flower vase/cups/shelf corners from image 2. Do not crop/zoom either input as a substitute for a moved camera. Use natural perspective/parallax. Do not add a wide lens, extra door or new window to fit things in.

LOCKED ARCHITECTURE:
Original cafe entry is one narrow centre wooden door between two glazed bays, under the burgundy awning. Original approach image 1 establishes its exact opening, mullions, hinges, sill and glazing. Keep that topology and door-leaf pose. Do not widen it into double doors, change mullion counts, move the entrance along the facade or replace the dark wood profiles. Only the leaf is already open; the frame and front wall never move.

LOCKED INTERIOR:
Inside is the SAME long wood-and-stone counter on the LEFT when entering, with the near glass pastry domes, the SAME clear vase of white flowers, cup stacks and service bell; the espresso machine is farther down the counter BEHIND the flower vase as established by image 2. Do not bring the machine forward just to keep it in frame. The same left-wall cabinets/jars, rear shelving, right-side small tables and cane chairs, cream plaster, timber ceiling beams, parquet floor and brass pendant fixtures stay where they are. Preserve distinct local shapes and texture details, not merely the same general style. Hidden or occluded objects may remain hidden. Do not invent a second street, a poster of the canal on the rear wall, extra exits, extra furniture, people or a new room.
The opening provides a genuine view into this room; do not flatten the entire interior behind the glass or on a single wall. Fixed doorframe occludes it correctly.
Same blue-hour dusk, interior electric lights ON, identical warm light sources and material colors. No relighting in this frame.
Output ONE clean photorealistic landscape 16:9 image, no labels, captions, arrows, border, split screen or collage.
